newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ranariddh, seeking to survive, tries to woo Manila.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh, seeking to survive, tries to woo Manila.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh flew into the Philippines on Sunday to hold talks with President Fidel Ramos on the fifth leg of an Asian tour to win diplomatic support.

"I'll see you after my meeting with the president," the prince told reporters on arrival from Bangkok. He received a low-key welcome at Manila airport from a Philippine official party led by foreign office chief of protocol, Ambassador Victor Garcia.
Foreign Undersecretary Rodolfo Severino, who is to meet Ranariddh later on Sunday, declined to say what specific subjects he or Ramos would discuss with the prince.
"He (Ramos) will listen to him...The president obviously has some ideas," he said.
Ranariddh's stop in the Philippines was his fifth on a tour of member countries of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Asked how ASEAN countries which Ranariddh has visited -- Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia -- reacted to the prince's campaign for support, Severino said: "They listened to him."
ASEAN was to have accepted Cambodia as a member last month but the group postponed its entry after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh in a coup.
Troops loyal to Hun Sen have been closing in on the last major position held by royalist forces in the country.
ASEAN comprises Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam and new members Laos and Burma.
Ranariddh may leave Manila on Monday night, officials said.
